title: Differential stability of alternating stages
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $K$ a bicomplex of $A$-modules with commuting horizontal and vertical differentials of bidegrees $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and let $T$ be its coproduct total cochain complex, with total differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$. Suppose every column $p>0$ is zero. For each $j\in\mathbf N$, fix a short complex $S_j=(U_j\xrightarrow{f_j}B_j\xrightarrow{g_j}V_j)$ of cochain complexes and an isomorphism $e_j:B_j\cong K^{-j,\bullet}$. For $n\in\mathbf N$ and $k\in\mathbf Z$, define the submodule $M_n^k$ of $T^k$ as the sum, over $j\in\mathbf N$, of the full image of $K^{-j,k+j}\to T^k$ if $2j+2\le n$, and the image of $U_j^{k+j}\xrightarrow{f_j}B_j^{k+j}\xrightarrow{e_j}K^{-j,k+j}\to T^k$ if $2j+1\le n$; omit a summand when its inequality fails. Then $d_T^{k,l}(M_n^k)\subseteq M_n^l$ for all $n,k,l$. Restricting $d_T$ gives actual subcomplexes $F_n$ of $T$. The construction also has $M_0^k=0$, $M_n^k\subseteq M_m^k$ when $n\le m$, monomorphic inclusions $F_n\to T$, and compatible successive inclusions.

source.place: Tag 09KP, proof, alternating two-step column filtration (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09KP)

proof.text: Define the full and lower image submodules by their canonical total-degree injections. Their threshold formula gives stage zero and monotonicity by natural-number arithmetic.

Check differential stability on each image generator. The vertical part preserves the full column or lower image because the lower arrow is a cochain map. The horizontal part for j>0 lands in the earlier full column j-1, whose threshold 2j is at most the lower threshold 2j+1. For j=0 it lands in a positive zero column. Closure of submodules under sums and signs extends to the supremum.

Restrict the actual total differential to the stable submodules. Its shape and square-zero equations follow from those of the total complex by taking underlying elements. Subtype inclusions are degreewise injective and give monomorphisms of complexes; nested submodule inclusions commute with them.
